name: Question 2
problem:
Find the limit ${lim}_{t\to 3}[f(t)\cdot g(t)]$ given that $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are defined as:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =\sqrt{t}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡(t-2)\,j+t\,k \\ g(t) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(t-2)\,i+\frac{t-{t}^{2}}{1-t}\,j+2\,k\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
First, we find the limit of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 3}f(t) & =({lim}_{t\to 3}\sqrt{t})\,i+({lim}_{t\to 3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(t-2))\,j+({lim}_{t\to 3}t)\,k \\  & =\sqrt{3}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡(3-2)\,j+3\,k \\  & =\sqrt{3}\,i+0\,j+3\,k \\  & =\sqrt{3}\,i+3\,k \\ {lim}_{t\to 3}g(t) & =({lim}_{t\to 3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(t-2))\,i+({lim}_{t\to 3}\frac{t-{t}^{2}}{1-t})\,j+({lim}_{t\to 3}2)\,k \\  & =({lim}_{t\to 3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(t-2))\,i+({lim}_{t\to 3}\frac{t(1-t)}{1-t})\,j+({lim}_{t\to 3}2)\,k \\  & =({lim}_{t\to 3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(t-2))\,i+({lim}_{t\to 3}t)\,j+({lim}_{t\to 3}2)\,k \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3-2)\,i+3\,j+2\,k \\  & =0\,i+3\,j+2\,k \\  & =3\,j+2\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 3}[f(t)\cdot g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to 3}f(t)\cdot {lim}_{t\to 3}g(t) \\  & =(\sqrt{3}\,i+3\,k)\cdot (3\,j+2\,k) \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot 0+0\cdot 3+3\cdot 2 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

First, we find the limit of each function:

limt→3f(t)=(limt→3t)i+(limt→3ln⁡(t−2))j+(limt→3t)k=3i+ln⁡(3−2)j+3k=3i+0j+3k=3i+3klimt→3g(t)=(limt→3ln⁡(t−2))i+(limt→3t−t21−t)j+(limt→32)k=(limt→3ln⁡(t−2))i+(limt→3t(1−t)1−t)j+(limt→32)k=(limt→3ln⁡(t−2))i+(limt→3t)j+(limt→32)k=ln⁡(3−2)i+3j+2k=0i+3j+2k=3j+2k

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

limt→3[f(t)⋅g(t)]=limt→3f(t)⋅limt→3g(t)=(3i+3k)⋅(3j+2k)=3⋅0+0⋅3+3⋅2=6.
